terminal_target_provenance.rule: TARGET vs TRAJECTORY, recorded separately: the terminal touch state is ANCHORED to the v3 gate3 seed (a physics-verified pose: registration anchor + terminal alignment both aim at it), so the acceptance criteria are decided by that seed, NOT by HaMeR. The constrained solve's signed rate band is the second, command-side low-pass.

servo_winding_position.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per finger joint: (1) excess beyond jnt_range <= |forcerange|/kp, (2) at most 3 consecutive control frames (150 ms at 20 Hz), (3) the transient is elastic wind-up: there is a contact torque on that DoF, the actuator is not on its force limit while it happens, and kp*(ctrl-qpos) accounts for the whole non-actuator load on the DoF to 5%. An excursion during saturation is never exempted, and neither is one on a freely drifting joint.

findings.finding: v5+ finger springs exceed the finger servo static hold envelope for the gate3 seed's deep curls
findings.evidence: spring torque 0.4*(q-0.6) at the seed: ffj2_r needs 0.279 Nm vs forcerange 0.094 Nm (mfj2_r 0.354/0.094, mfj1_r 0.247/0.104, thj3_r 0.197/0.030; left ffj1 0.279/0.105, rfj2 0.251/0.094 ...). r8 executed terminal: right best pad ~22 mm high on the face (band penalty) with 32 end-face contact frames; left ~8 mm high with 39 -- both hands still ride above the mid band (v14 baseline: right 14.9 mm, left SEATED 0.29 mm; the v20 follower pads are the suspected compliance path, see r7_comparison). The r8 holdable-band command clamp cut the gate4 realised over-range 39.3 -> 6.8 mrad.
findings.consequence: the executed terminal cannot reproduce the seed's deep curls; the >=2-pad terminal criterion needs either servo/spring re-budget (scene generation) or a hold-feasible seed family

findings.finding: the registered approach dipped below the table (gate3, zero hand-vs-support contact over the whole clip) -- RESOLVED (r8)
findings.evidence: r8 approach-height budget (clamp clearance 30 -> 60 mm): ZERO support-contact frames on BOTH hands (r7: right 12 [5-18], left 25 [32, 243-265]; r5n: 12/23). The video's own left-hand rest pose sits at table height and the MANO depth axis is unusable (4.8-6.3 m weak-perspective); the deeper clamp lift covers the tracking deficit
findings.consequence: gate3 is green for the first time since round 2; the cost is a slightly larger early-approach execution deviation (gate5 left 0.142 -> 0.152 m)

findings.finding: box disturbance at the terminal stays resolved on v25 (r8): the recorded object pose stays upright through the replay
findings.evidence: terminal box tilt 1.39 deg from identity, 6.3 mm total displacement (the base-y corridor is world-centred per mount under the r8 semantics; the right mount's centred mean is structurally unreachable -- the measured lateral path eats the slide range -- and the search box clamps to the nearest feasible base, disclosed in terminal_target_provenance.r8_execution_fixes)
findings.consequence: the executed terminal rect distances are measured against a live, near-upright box; no further corridor work is verdict-bearing

trajectory_error.metric_definition_caveat: the reference curve is the HAND BOUNDING-BOX centre (the only per-frame pixel signal in the npz), not the wrist landmark: the box centre moves OPPOSITE to the wrist when fingers curl (an articulation lever), so this metric is an UPPER BOUND on true wrist tracking error. The round-4b tradeoff sweep (SG windows 5/9/15/21/31 frames) moves it by <2% of the span (0.329/0.201 -> 0.320/0.193) -- the residual is SYSTEMATIC, not jitter, and no filter setting can close it. A wrist-landmark pixel reference (MediaPipe wrist) is the fix and is perception scope.

smoothness_comparison.metric: mean |second difference| of the realised wrist joints (6 slides+hinges) per control second, over the video grid; frozen before this run
